beliefs.practice: Never put the DocumentDB/MongoDB connection string or OpenAI API key in source code or checked-in files; always read them from environment variables (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY) and provide a .env.example with placeholders only.

Use a single shared MongoClient (pymongo.MongoClient) instance per process and reuse it for all requests; create it at app startup and close it on shutdown to avoid connection churn and socket exhaustion.
Do not store large binary image data in DocumentDB; store only metadata and a URI reference to the image in blob/object storage (e.g., Azure Blob Storage) to keep documents small and fast.

Store embeddings as numeric arrays (number[]) in documents when using the provider's native vector indexes (rather than as BSON binary blobs) because native vector indexes generally require numeric arrays and may not index binary-encoded vectors.
Normalize embeddings to unit length at insert time if you plan to use cosine similarity, so you can use dot product on normalized vectors as the similarity measure.
Compute embeddings once at write time and store them with the document; avoid recomputing embeddings on every query to reduce cost and latency.

Create appropriate B-tree indexes on metadata fields used as filters (e.g., modality, body_part) and use compound queries (vector search + metadata filters) so filter predicates are applied efficiently on retrieved candidates.

Use a two-stage query pattern: (1) use the vector index to get a limited set of nearest-neighbour candidates, (2) re-rank or filter those candidates in-app (or with an additional DB filter) combining metadata and relevance.

When creating vector indexes (IVF/HNSW), set explicit index parameters (dimension, metric like cosine or euclidean, nlist/hnsw parameters) appropriate for your vector dimensionality and dataset size; test with explain() to validate performance.
Limit result set sizes (use limit, pagination) and avoid unbounded sorts on large result sets; for semantic search return a small top-K (e.g., top 10) and implement cursor-based paging if needed.

Apply retries with exponential backoff for transient network errors and transient server errors (e.g., 5xx, network timeouts); make retries idempotent for operations that need it (use idempotency or client-generated IDs).

Use appropriate client timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) and monitor connection pool metrics; tune pool size to match concurrency and cluster capacity to avoid connection saturation.
Grant the application a least-privilege database user (a role limited to the sample database, e.g., readWrite on sample_healthcare_04) instead of using an admin/root credential.
Use TLS/SSL for all connections to the DocumentDB cluster and ensure the driver verifies server certificates to protect PHI in transit.

Keep documents small (well under the DB max document size), avoid embedding large arrays that grow unbounded (e.g., crowding embeddings into huge arrays), and consider bucketing or referencing for large collections.

Prefer storing only structured metadata fields (modality, body_part, study_date, clinical_finding) and add a JSON Schema validator on the collection to enforce field types and vector dimension/length constraints at insert time.
Monitor query performance and index usage; use explain() on representative queries and adjust indexes or index parameters if scans or long execution times appear.

Use server-side or managed encryption and key-management (e.g., Azure-managed keys or customer-managed keys) for at-rest encryption of sensitive medical metadata and credentials; do not rely solely on application-layer encryption unless required.
Protect against injection attacks by validating and sanitizing user-supplied filter values and disallowing raw JSON fragments in API query parameters that could be used to inject operators.

If tooling for index creation (MCP/CLI) fails, fall back to using the driver (pymongo.create_index or createIndexes command) to create the vector index and then verify with listIndexes or the provider's admin tooling.
For demos, seed deterministic pseudo-embeddings when API keys are unavailable, but document this clearly and ensure production paths compute real embeddings with proper secrets management.

Tune provisioning: use autoscale or appropriate RU/throughput settings for the collection depending on expected query/write load and vector-index maintenance cost; avoid underprovisioning which causes throttling.

Prefer application-side re-ranking and final scoring rather than complex in-DB scripting; run the vector search to retrieve candidates then compute any custom clinical-scoring logic in-app for clarity and safety.
Log queries, latencies, and index-creation events but never log PHI or raw clinical findings; make sure logging and telemetry scrub or omit any patient-identifying fields.
Rotate keys and use a secret manager (e.g., Azure Key Vault) for database credentials and API keys; automate rotation and avoid long-lived static secrets in environment files for production.
